signaling_summary: AHCI itself is a fully-digital register / memory-structure specification. The analog/mixed-signal content lives one layer below — in the integrated SATA Transport / Link / PHY layers (defined in Serial ATA 2.6, referenced as out-of-scope by AHCI 1.3.1 §1.3). Per port, the PHY drives a low-voltage differential (LVDS-class) signaling pair A+/A- (TX) and senses B+/B- (RX) at line rates of 1.5 Gbps (Gen 1) / 3.0 Gbps (Gen 2) / 6.0 Gbps (Gen 3), with 8b/10b embedded clocking, on-chip CDR (clock-and-data-recovery), de-emphasis on TX, equalization on RX, spread-spectrum-clocking tolerance, and Out-Of-Band (OOB) burst detection for COMRESET / COMINIT / COMWAKE. The AHCI 1.3.1 sideband DEVSLP signal is a slow-rate digital sideband (CMOS) but its assertion is gated by the analog PHY power state.

voltage_classes.level: Implementation-defined (typ 3.3 V / 1.8 V / 1.2 V depending on board)

oob_signaling_summary: OOB bursts are low-frequency envelopes of ALIGN primitives at the line rate, separated by idle periods. COMRESET, COMINIT, and COMWAKE differ only in burst-to-idle ratios and are detected by analog envelope detectors in the PHY. After OOB completes, the PHY locks bit + word, exchanges TS1/TS2 training primitives equivalent, negotiates speed (highest common Gen), and reports PhyRdy = 1 to the Link layer.
notes: AHCI is explicitly out of scope for the PHY analog characteristics (AHCI 1.3.1 §1.3 — 'AHCI does not contain information relevant to implementing the Transport, Link or Phy layers of Serial ATA as this is wholly described in the Serial ATA 1.0a / 2.6 specification.'). Implementations integrate a hard SATA PHY macro per port; the digital AHCI register block sees only PhyRdy / PhyOnline / Speed[1:0] / IPM-state vectors back from the PHY.
